MQ01.observed: The first five direct answers select the released key B and correctly identify the lesser sac. Several explanations phrase the gastrohepatic route as the required/default laparoscopic pancreatic route, rather than the best available option in this question.
MQ01.concern: Post hoc primary surgical series describe gastrocolic access. That ligament is absent from the options. A case-series alternative does not invalidate possible gastrohepatic access or authorize changing the published key, but it limits universal operative-route assertions. Qwen's agent response also labels the gastrohepatic portion as the free edge; the post hoc expert chapter distinguishes the hepatoduodenal free edge.

MQ02.observed: Read direct Kimi, MiMo, Qwen and Gemma responses choose recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and connect postoperative hoarseness to inferior thyroid artery proximity. Their explanations generally discriminate the other nerve options.
MQ02.concern: Broad claims about a single safe/unsafe artery-ligation location exceed what this examination vignette establishes. Primary anatomy data describe variable nerve-artery relationships, so these short explanations are not operative instructions.

MQ03.observed: All five read direct justifications choose the released key A and connect prolonged multi-domain worry to sleep, tension, irritability and attention symptoms.
MQ03.concern: Several call complete DSM criteria definitively met even though the compressed vignette does not explicitly establish every criterion, including difficulty controlling worry or frequency. Qwen uses duration as an argument against adjustment disorder without explaining persistence/stressor conditions. These are qualitative precision concerns, not a replacement key.

MQ04.concern: Separate the released-option discrepancy from the plausibility of the disease explanation. MQ05.concern: GLM's triad wording substitutes the preceding trigger for urethritis. MQ07.observed: All five read direct responses choose the published A and connect resistant hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis to aldosterone excess.
MQ07.concern: GLM says renin-mediated hypoperfusion 'is suppressed here', although the case supplies no renin result. Several explanations do not acknowledge the potassium effects of the stated hydrochlorothiazide. These explanation concerns do not change key scoring.

MQ08.concern: The stem describes several weeks, whereas several explanations assert chronic tubulointerstitial damage as established. MQ09.concern: The explanations are concise and generally distinguish environmental disinfection from ordinary alcohol cleaning. records.answer_excerpt: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) is closely related to the inferior thyroid artery, often crossing it or running in close proximity within the tracheoesophageal groove. During thyroid surgery, ligation of the inferior thyroid artery carries a significant risk of injury to the RLN. Damage to the RLN leads to paralysis of the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (excluding the cricothyroid), resulting in vocal cord dysfunction and the characteristic symptom of hoarseness.
